definition_en: something you say when you leave someone or when someone leaves you
core_image: 站在门口挥着手，看着对方走远
scene: 校车开动时，孩子们隔着车窗向老师挥手道别。The children waved goodbye to their teacher as the school bus pulled away.
sceneCN: 这里 goodbye 是「再见」（第 1 个义项：分别时说的话）；句意：校车开走时，孩子们隔着车窗向老师挥手说再见。

derivatives.zh: goodbye 的截短形式，义为「再见」
美式拼写变体，义同「告别」

senses.title: A word said when leaving
senses.definition: a word you say to someone when one of you is leaving
senses.definitionCN: 当其中一方要离开时所说的话
senses.example: She said goodbye and closed the door softly.
senses.exampleCN: 她说了声再见，轻轻关上了门。
senses.why: The word began as a blessing, God be with you, so the core image is a parting wish sent after someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一句祝福「愿上帝与你同在」，所以核心画面是朝着对方背影送出的一句祝愿。

senses.title: The act of parting
senses.definition: the moment or occasion when people part from each other
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此分开的那一刻或场合
senses.example: It was a sad goodbye at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 机场的那场告别令人伤感。
senses.why: The spoken word becomes a countable noun for the whole scene of leaving.
senses.whyCN: 这句说出口的话变成一个可数名词，指整个分别的场面。

senses.title: To give something up
senses.definition: used in phrases meaning to accept the loss of something and stop expecting it
senses.definitionCN: 用于某些说法，表示接受失去某物并不再指望
senses.example: The villagers said goodbye to their old market that spring.
senses.exampleCN: 那年春天，村民们与他们的旧集市告别了。
senses.why: Leaving a person develops into leaving a thing, so goodbye can mark any permanent parting.
senses.whyCN: 与人分别发展为与事物分别，因此 goodbye 可以标记任何永久性的离开。

intro.en: Goodbye is a worn-down contraction of the blessing God be with you, shortened over several centuries.
intro.cn: goodbye 是祝福语「愿上帝与你同在」在数百年间不断缩略形成的词。

items.en: The blessing phrasing is built from God, be, with, and you, all native words.
items.cn: 这句祝福由 God、be、with、you 这些本土词组成。

items.en: The full phrase is slurred in speech into forms such as godbwye.
items.cn: 十六世纪，完整短语在口语中被连读成 godbwye 之类的形式。

items.en: Writers begin to spell the contraction as good-bye, treating good as the ordinary word.
items.cn: 写作者开始把这个缩略形式拼作 good-bye，把 good 当成普通的词。

items.en: Goodbye settles as the standard spelling for the parting word.
items.cn: 十八世纪，goodbye 固定为告别用语的标准拼写。

items.en: The word now serves as both an interjection and a countable noun.
items.cn: 现在这个词既作感叹词，也作可数名词。

note.en: Goodbye has a shortened twin in bye, and it stands beside other words of parting.
note.cn: goodbye 有一个截短的孪生形式 bye，并与其它表示告别的词相邻。

entries.definition: a short informal way of saying goodbye
entries.definitionCN: 再见，是 goodbye 的简短口语形式

entries.definition: an American spelling variant of goodbye
a daytime parting greeting
entries.definitionCN: 白天的告别问候，与 goodbye 同为 good 复合词

entries.definition: an old-fashioned or formal word for goodbye
entries.definitionCN: 告别，语气正式且偏旧式

entries.definition: the act of separating from someone
entries.definitionCN: 分别；离别，是书面语名词

entries.definition: an informal way of saying goodbye
entries.definitionCN: 回头见，是非正式告别语

normalIntro.en: The word is a squeezed blessing, so the best memory hook is the phrase it came from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是被挤短的祝福语，最好的记忆钩子就是它原本的那句话。

normal.en: God be with you, said quickly, wears down into goodbye.
normal.cn: God be with you 说得很快，就磨成了 goodbye。

normal.en: The spelling split as good-bye shows how good was later read into it.
normal.cn: 曾写作 good-bye 的拼法说明后来的人把 good 读了进去。

normal.en: Bye is the same word with the front cut off.
normal.cn: bye 是同一个词被切掉了前半部分。

normal.en: Wave goodbye and say goodbye are the two most common pairings.
normal.cn: wave goodbye 与 say goodbye 是两个最常见的搭配。

normal.en: As a noun it takes a plural: two quick goodbyes at the station.
normal.cn: 作名词时有复数：在车站匆匆道了两次别。

abstract.en: Picture a hand still raised after the bus has turned the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象巴士转过街角后，那只手还举在半空。

abstract.en: See a platform slowly emptying after a train leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象列车开走后，站台慢慢空下来。

abstract.en: Think of a door closing gently on a familiar room.
abstract.cn: 想一扇门在熟悉的房间前轻轻合上。

examples.en: He waved goodbye and walked to the gate.
We said our goodbyes at the station.
Say goodbye to the old bike; it is going to the scrap yard.
examples.cn: 跟那辆旧自行车告别吧，它要去废品站了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「固的拜」——想象关系很稳固的朋友在门口拜别；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由祝福语 God be with you 在十六世纪起的口语连读逐步缩略而成，good 是后来按拼写重新解释出来的成分。

sensesIntro.en: A blessing spoken at parting turns into the parting word itself and then into the whole occasion of leaving.
sensesIntro.cn: 分别时说的一句祝福，先变成告别用语本身，再变成整个离开的场面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand still raised while the other person walks away.
core.cn: 核心意象：对方走远了，手还举着。

branches.en: The blessing becomes the everyday word for leaving.
branches.cn: 那句祝福成为日常告别用语。

branches.en: The spoken word names the whole scene of parting.
branches.cn: 说出口的词转而指整个分别场面。

branches.en: Leaving a person extends to leaving a thing behind.
branches.cn: 与人分别延伸到与事物分别。

branches.en: Word and occasion are two sides of one parting.
branches.cn: 话语与场合是同一次分别的两面。

branches.en: Both involve accepting that something is now gone.
branches.cn: 两者都包含承认某物已经不在。

intro.en: Goodbye looks like a compound but is really a worn phrase, so its parts are historical rather than productive.
intro.cn: goodbye 看起来像复合词，实际上是磨旧的短语，其成分属历史遗留而非能产构词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; every piece is native English or Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分，每个部分都来自英语本土或日耳曼语。

items.meaning: the deity addressed in the blessing
items.example: God is the first word of the original phrase.
items.exampleCN: God 是原来那句话的第一个词。

items.example: Be carries the wish in God be with you.
items.exampleCN: be 承载了「愿……同在」的愿望。

items.example: With links the person and the blessing.
items.exampleCN: with 把人与其祝福连在一起。

items.example: You is the last word before the phrase collapsed.
items.exampleCN: you 是短语缩合前的最后一个词。

items.meaning: good, read in later by folk etymology
items.meaningCN: 好的，后来被民间词源重新读入
items.example: Good- is not in the original blessing.
items.exampleCN: good- 并不在最初的祝福语里。

items.meaning: the compressed ending of the phrase
items.meaningCN: 短语压缩后留下的词尾
items.example: The ending -bye is all that is left of be with ye.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -bye 是 be with ye 压缩后的残留。

items.example: Bye drops the first element entirely.
items.exampleCN: bye 把第一个成分整个丢掉。

items.example: Goodby keeps the compound shape without the hyphen.
items.exampleCN: goodby 去掉了连字符，保留复合外形。

definition_zh: 请；使高兴；使满意；随……的意
definition_en: used to ask politely, or to make someone happy and satisfied
core_image: 双手在胸前合起，微微低头请人帮忙
scene: 他敲了敲门，礼貌地说了声请进。He knocked on the door and said please come in.
sceneCN: 这里 please 是「请」（第 1 个义项：礼貌地请求或邀请）；句意：他敲了敲门，客气地说了声请进。

derivatives.zh: please 加 -ed 构成，义为「高兴的；满意的」
与 please 同出拉丁语 placere，义为「愉快；乐趣」
与 please 同源，义为「令人愉快的」
pleasant 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「令人不快的」

senses.title: Used to ask politely
senses.definition: a polite word added to a request, an invitation, or an instruction
senses.definitionCN: 加在请求、邀请或指示中表示礼貌的词
senses.example: Please sit down and wait a moment.
senses.why: The Latin verb means to be agreeable, so the polite word originally puts the request in a form the other person can accept.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使人满意」，所以这个礼貌用词从一开始就是给对方一个愿意接受的形式。

senses.title: To make someone happy
senses.definition: to give someone pleasure or satisfaction
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人愉快或满足
senses.example: The little gift pleased her more than anything expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 这件小礼物比任何昂贵的东西都让她高兴。
senses.why: If the word means agreeable, the verb names the act of making someone agreeable or content.
senses.whyCN: 「使人满意」这个动作说的正是让某人心里舒服、愿意接受，所以动词义是「使高兴、使满意」。

senses.title: To want or choose
senses.definition: to be someone's wish or choice, used in set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人的意愿或选择，多用于固定说法
senses.example: Take as many apples as you please.
senses.exampleCN: 苹果你想拿多少就拿多少。
senses.why: Whatever pleases a person is what they choose, so the verb slides into the sense of wanting.
senses.whyCN: 一个人愿意要什么，就会被什么「取悦」，于是动词自然滑向「想要、愿意」的意思。

intro.en: Please comes from Old French plaisir, from Latin placere, to be agreeable or to please.
intro.cn: please 来自古法语 plaisir，源自拉丁语 placere「令人满意、使人愉快」。

items.en: Placere means to be pleasing or acceptable, and gives placid and complacent.
items.cn: placere 意为令人愉快、可接受，也产生了 placid 与 complacent。

items.en: The noun placitum names what has been agreed or decided.
items.cn: 名词 placitum 指已经议定或决定的事。

items.en: Plaisir means to please and also the feeling of pleasure.
items.cn: 古法语 plaisir 既表示使高兴，也表示愉快的感受。

items.en: English please first means to be pleasing to someone.
items.cn: 英语 please 最初表示「使某人愉快」。

items.en: The polite use, added to requests, becomes fixed in everyday speech.
items.cn: 十七世纪，加在请求中的礼貌用法在日常口语中固定下来。

items.en: The adverb use now dominates, while the verb survives in pleased and pleasing.
items.cn: 如今副词用法占据主导，动词义则保留在 pleased 与 pleasing 中。

note.en: Please has a large Latin family, and its polite use pairs with the verbs of satisfying.
note.cn: please 有一个庞大的拉丁词族，其礼貌用法与表示「使人满意」的动词呼应。

entries.definition: happy or satisfied about something
entries.definitionCN: 高兴的；满意的，由 please 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: a feeling of happiness or enjoyment
entries.definitionCN: 愉快；乐趣，与 please 同出拉丁语 placere

entries.definition: enjoyable and giving pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的，与 please 同源

entries.definition: to make someone content by meeting a need
entries.definitionCN: 使满意；满足，比 please 更强调需求被满足

entries.definition: to give someone great pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 使高兴；使喜悦，语气比 please 强

entries.definition: to please someone greatly by being attractive

normalIntro.en: The family runs from placere through please to pleasure and pleasant, all about being agreeable.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族从 placere 经 please 到 pleasure 与 pleasant，核心都是「令人愉快」。

normal.en: Pleasure and pleasant keep the same Latin stem as please.
normal.cn: pleasure 与 pleasant 与 please 共享同一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: Add -ed for pleased and -ing for pleasing, two everyday adjectives.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 得 pleased，加 -ing 得 pleasing，两者都是常用形容词。

normal.en: As a polite word it usually sits at the start or the end of a request.
normal.cn: 作礼貌用词时，它通常位于请求的开头或结尾。

normal.en: Yes please is the polite way to accept an offer.
normal.cn: yes please 是接受别人好意时的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Please yourself sounds a little cool or annoyed.
normal.cn: please yourself 听起来有点冷淡或不耐烦。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressed together at chest height.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在胸前合十。

abstract.en: See a shopkeeper sliding a paper bag across the counter with a nod.
abstract.cn: 想象店主点点头，把纸袋推过柜台。

abstract.en: Think of a smile that appears because someone got what they wanted.
abstract.cn: 想一个因为如愿而浮起的笑容。

examples.en: Please close the window before you leave.
The result pleased everyone in the team.
examples.cn: 这个结果让队里每个人都很满意。

examples.en: She is pleased with her new room.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普利兹」——想象用很普及的礼貌语请人帮忙；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 plaisir，源自拉丁语 placere（令人满意、使人愉快）。

sensesIntro.en: Being agreeable gives the polite request, the act of satisfying someone, and the sense of doing as one wishes.
sensesIntro.cn: 「令人满意」给出礼貌请求、使人满意这个动作，以及「随心所欲」的含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands pressed together in a polite request.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸前合起的双手，客气地请求。

branches.en: The polite request is the most frequent modern use.
branches.cn: 礼貌请求是今天最常见的用法。

branches.en: The verb names giving someone satisfaction.
branches.cn: 动词义指给予某人满足。

branches.en: What pleases a person is what they choose to take.
branches.cn: 让人满意的东西，就是人愿意拿的东西。

branches.en: Both rest on the idea of making things agreeable.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在「让事情变得可接受」上。

branches.en: Satisfaction and personal wish are close neighbours.
branches.cn: 满足与个人意愿是近邻。

intro.en: Please is a Latin verb shortened by French, and its related words keep the plain stem pleas-.
intro.cn: please 是被法语缩短的拉丁动词，其相关词保留着朴素的词干 pleas-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base plac- means pleasing or agreeable, and it survives in placid, pleasant, and pleasure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 plac- 表示「令人愉快的」，在 placid、pleasant、pleasure 中仍然留存。

items.example: The pleas- stem carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pleas- 词干承载着整个词族。

items.example: Placere is the Latin verb behind the root.
items.exampleCN: placere 是词根背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: Pleased describes someone who has been satisfied.
items.exampleCN: pleased 描述已经感到满意的人。

items.example: Pleasing describes something that gives pleasure.
items.exampleCN: pleasing 描述给人愉快的事物。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Pleasure names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: pleasure 指愉快这种感受本身。

items.example: Pleasant means having a pleasing quality.
items.exampleCN: pleasant 意为「具有令人愉快性质的」。

items.example: Placid keeps the same plac- base.
items.exampleCN: placid 保留同一个 plac- 词基。

items.example: Complacent adds com- to the same base.
items.exampleCN: complacent 在同一个词基前加了 com-。

definition_en: to tell someone that you are grateful for something they have done
core_image: 接过别人递来的东西，低头说一声谢
scene: 老人接过水杯，向学生点头致谢。The old man took the cup and thanked the student with a nod.
sceneCN: 这里 thank 是「感谢」（第 1 个义项：向人表达谢意）；句意：老人接过水杯，向学生点头表示感谢。

derivatives.zh: thank 加 -ful 构成，义为「感激的」
thank 加 -less 构成，义为「得不到感谢的；不值得感激的」
thank 的复数名词化，义为「谢意」

senses.title: To tell someone you are grateful
senses.definition: to say that you are grateful to someone for something they gave or did
senses.definitionCN: 就别人给予或所做之事向对方表示感激
senses.example: She thanked the driver for waiting.
senses.why: The Old English noun behind the verb means thought or good will, so thanking is giving someone the thought that they were kind.
senses.whyCN: 动词背后的古英语名词意为「想法、善意」，所以道谢就是把「你很好心」这个念头说给对方。

senses.title: Words or feelings of gratitude
senses.definition: an expression of gratitude, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 感激的表达，通常用复数形式
senses.example: She sent her thanks to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她向整个团队表达了谢意。
senses.why: The verb's plural form works as a noun, naming the spoken or written thanks themselves.
senses.whyCN: 动词的复数形式被拿来当名词用，指的就是说出口或写下来的那些感谢话。

senses.title: Because of, as a result of
senses.definition: used in the phrase thanks to to say that something good happened because of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于 thanks to 这一说法，表示好事因某人或某物而发生
senses.example: Thanks to the early rain, the garden looks green again.
senses.exampleCN: 多亏了那场早雨，花园又绿了起来。
senses.why: If someone caused a good result, gratitude is owed to them, and the phrase turns that debt into a cause.
senses.whyCN: 如果某件事带来了好结果，感激就落到促成它的人身上，短语便把这份亏欠转成「多亏、归功于」。

intro.en: Thank comes from Old English thancian, related to the noun thanc, thought or gratitude.
intro.cn: thank 来自古英语 thancian，与名词 thanc（想法、感激）相关。

items.en: Thanc means thought, good will, or gratitude.
items.cn: thanc 意为想法、善意或感激。

items.en: Thancian is the verb meaning to give thanks or to be grateful.
items.cn: thancian 是表示致谢、心怀感激的动词。

items.en: The verb becomes thank, and the plural thanks becomes a noun for gratitude.
items.cn: 中古英语中动词演变为 thank，复数 thanks 成为表示谢意的名词。

items.en: Thank you settles as the fixed polite formula.
items.cn: thank you 固定为礼貌用语。

items.en: Thanks to develops the sense of owing a good result to someone.
items.cn: thanks to 发展出「把好结果归功于某人」的含义。

note.en: Thank has a small native family, and it stands beside the vocabulary of gratitude.
note.cn: thank 有一个小的本土词族，并与表示感激的词汇相邻。

entries.definition: words expressing gratitude
entries.definitionCN: 谢意；感谢的话，是 thank 的复数名词化

entries.definition: feeling grateful
not producing thanks or not appreciated
entries.definitionCN: 得不到感谢的；白费力气的

entries.definition: to be grateful for something
entries.definitionCN: 感激；赏识，语气比 thank 更正式

entries.definition: the feeling of being grateful
to show that you have received something

normalIntro.en: Thank is connected to the old word for thought, so gratitude begins as holding someone in mind.
normalIntro.cn: thank 与表示「想法」的古词相连，感激最初就是把对方放在心上。

normal.en: The old noun meant thought or good will, so thanks is good will spoken aloud.
normal.cn: 古名词意为想法或善意，所以道谢就是把善意说出来。

normal.en: Add -ful for thankful and -less for thankless.
normal.cn: 加 -ful 得 thankful，加 -less 得 thankless。

normal.en: The plural thanks works as a noun, as in many thanks.
normal.cn: 复数 thanks 作名词用，如 many thanks。

normal.en: Thank someone for something, not to something.
normal.cn: 句型是 thank someone for something，介词用 for。

normal.en: Thanks to introduces a cause, and it usually points to a good one.
normal.cn: thanks to 引出原因，通常指好的原因。

abstract.en: Picture both hands taking a cup and a small bow of the head.
abstract.cn: 想象双手接过杯子，同时轻轻低头。

abstract.en: See a card with two short lines written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着两行短句的卡片。

abstract.en: Think of a warm nod exchanged at a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想门口互相点头致意的那一刻。

examples.en: I thanked her for helping with the boxes.
Many thanks for your kind reply.
examples.cn: 非常感谢您的亲切回复。

examples.en: Thanks to the new road, the trip takes half the time.
examples.cn: 多亏了这条新路，行程时间缩短了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三克」——想象收到三克重的小礼物也要认真道谢；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 thancian，与名词 thanc（想法、善意、感激）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Holding someone in grateful thought becomes the verb, the plural noun, and the phrase that credits a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 把对方放在感激的念头里，长成动词、复数名词，以及把结果归功于某方的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bow while receiving something.
core.cn: 核心意象：接过东西时轻轻低头。

branches.en: The verb speaks the good will out loud.
branches.cn: 动词义把这份善意说出口。

branches.en: The plural noun names the words themselves.
branches.cn: 复数名词指这些话语本身。

branches.en: Gratitude turns into credit when a good result is traced to someone.
branches.cn: 当好结果被追溯到某人身上，感激就变成归功。

branches.en: Saying thanks and the thanks said are the same act.
branches.cn: 道谢与所说的谢意是同一个行为。

branches.en: Both keep the idea of a debt of good will.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了「善意之债」的观念。

intro.en: Thank is a native stem that takes familiar English endings rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: thank 是本土词干，接的是常见英语词尾，而不是拉丁词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in thank; its relatives come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: thank 没有拉丁成分，其同族词来自古英语。

items.example: The stem thank carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 thank 承载整个词族。

items.example: Thanks works as a plural noun.
items.exampleCN: thanks 作复数名词使用。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词词尾
items.example: Thanked marks the past tense.
items.exampleCN: thanked 标记过去式。

items.example: Thanking is the present participle.
items.exampleCN: thanking 是现在分词。

items.example: Thankful means full of gratitude.
items.exampleCN: thankful 意为「满怀感激的」。

items.example: Thankless means receiving no thanks.
items.exampleCN: thankless 意为「得不到感谢的」。

items.example: Thanc is the noun behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: thanc 是动词背后的名词。

items.example: Thancian is the Old English ancestor of thank.
items.exampleCN: thancian 是 thank 的古英语祖先。

definition_zh: 抱歉的；难过的；遗憾的；糟糕的
definition_en: feeling sad about something you did, or feeling pity for someone
core_image: 低着头，手不知该往哪里放
scene: 他不小心踩到别人的脚，立刻低声道歉。He stepped on her foot by accident and said sorry at once.
sceneCN: 这里 sorry 是「抱歉的」（第 1 个义项：因做错事而表示歉意）；句意：他不小心踩到她的脚，立刻说了抱歉。

pos.zh: 抱歉的；难过的；遗憾的；糟糕的

derivatives.zh: 与 sorry 同源，义为「悲伤；悲痛」
与 sorry 同源，义为「疼痛的」
sorry 加 -ly 构成，义为「可悲地；糟糕地」

senses.title: Feeling bad about something you did
senses.definition: feeling unhappy and guilty because you have done something wrong or hurt someone
senses.definitionCN: 因做错事或伤害他人而感到不快与内疚
senses.example: I am sorry for breaking your cup.
senses.exampleCN: 很抱歉打碎了你的杯子。
senses.why: The Old English word means full of pain, so the core image is a person carrying a small ache of guilt.
senses.whyCN: 古英语原词意为「满是痛楚的」，所以核心画面是一个人背着一点内疚的疼痛。

senses.title: Feeling pity for someone
senses.definition: feeling sadness and sympathy for someone in a bad situation
senses.definitionCN: 对处境不佳的人感到难过与同情
senses.example: I feel sorry for the children who missed the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 我为错过这次旅行的孩子们感到难过。
senses.why: The same ache can be felt for another person rather than for one's own fault.
senses.whyCN: 同一种疼痛可以不为自己的过错、而为别人的处境而生，于是有了「难过、同情」。

senses.title: Used to soften bad news
senses.definition: used politely when you must refuse, disagree, or give unwelcome information
senses.definitionCN: 在必须拒绝、反对或告知坏消息时使用的礼貌说法
senses.example: Sorry, the office is closed today.
senses.exampleCN: 很抱歉，办公室今天不办公。
senses.why: The apology is borrowed to cushion a refusal, even when no one is at fault.
senses.whyCN: 道歉的话被借来给拒绝垫一层软垫，即使并没有谁做错。

senses.title: Wretched or in a poor condition
senses.definition: describing something that is in a bad, neglected, or shameful state
senses.definitionCN: 形容事物处于糟糕、被忽视或令人难堪的状态
senses.example: The old shed was in a sorry state after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，那座旧棚屋状况很糟。
senses.why: Something that stirs pain when you look at it is itself called sorry, which shifts the feeling onto the object.
senses.whyCN: 一件让人看了就心里发疼的东西，本身也被叫作 sorry，感受就从人转移到了物上。

intro.en: Sorry comes from Old English sarig, from sar, sore or painful, and is related to sorrow.
intro.cn: sorry 来自古英语 sarig，源出 sar「疼痛的」，与 sorrow 同源。

items.en: Sar means sore or painful, both of a wound and of the mind.
items.cn: sar 意为疼痛的，既可指伤口，也可指心里的痛。

items.en: Sarig means distressed, grieved, or full of sorrow.
items.cn: sarig 意为痛苦的、悲伤的、满怀忧愁的。

items.en: The word becomes sory and covers grief as well as a poor condition.
items.cn: 中古英语中写作 sory，既指悲伤，也指糟糕的境况。

items.en: The apologetic use, I am sorry, becomes the everyday formula of apology.
items.cn: 十六世纪，I am sorry 成为日常道歉的固定说法。

items.en: The word also softens refusals and bad news, as in sorry, we are closed.
items.cn: 这个词也用于缓和拒绝与坏消息，如抱歉，我们打烊了。

note.en: Sorry shares its root with sorrow and sore, and it stands beside the vocabulary of apology.
note.cn: sorry 与 sorrow、sore 共享词根，并与道歉相关词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a feeling of deep sadness
entries.definitionCN: 悲伤；悲痛，与 sorry 同源

entries.definition: painful when touched
entries.definitionCN: 疼痛的，是 sorry 词根的形容词本义

entries.definition: in a poor or shameful way
entries.definitionCN: 可悲地；糟糕地，由 sorry 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: showing that you are sorry
feeling sorry about something done or not done
showing that you understand another person's sadness
entries.definitionCN: 同情的，与第二义项接近

normalIntro.en: The whole family starts from pain, so sorrow, sore, and sorry all share the same ache.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都从「疼痛」出发，sorrow、sore、sorry 共享同一份痛。

normal.en: Sore is the plain pain, sorrow the deep sadness, and sorry the small everyday ache.
normal.cn: sore 是身体的痛，sorrow 是深重的悲，sorry 是日常那一点歉疚。

normal.en: The pattern is be sorry for something or feel sorry for someone.
normal.cn: 句型是 be sorry for something 或 feel sorry for someone。

normal.en: Sorry at the start of a sentence often softens a refusal.
normal.cn: 句首的 sorry 常用来缓和拒绝。

normal.en: A sorry state means a neglected, shabby condition.
normal.cn: a sorry state 指被忽视、破败的状况。

normal.en: The comparative is sorrier, with the y changing to i.
normal.cn: 比较级是 sorrier，注意 y 变成 i。

abstract.en: Picture a child holding a broken cup behind their back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子把打碎的杯子藏在背后。

abstract.en: See a hand hovering near a shoulder, not quite touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手停在肩膀附近，却不敢落下。

abstract.en: Think of a fence leaning after a storm.
abstract.cn: 想一场风暴后歪倒的围栏。

examples.en: I am sorry that I missed your call.
examples.cn: 很抱歉我错过了你的电话。

examples.en: We felt sorry for the family who lost their home.
examples.cn: 我们为那户失去住房的家庭感到难过。

examples.en: Sorry, but the tickets are sold out.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫瑞」——想象扫兴的瑞丽之行只能向同伴道歉；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sarig（悲伤的、痛苦的），源出 sar（疼痛的），与 sorrow、sore 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One small ache of pain becomes guilt, sympathy, a softened refusal, and the description of a wrecked thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一点疼痛，长成内疚、同情、委婉的拒绝，以及对破败之物的形容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing still with lowered head.
core.cn: 核心意象：低着头站着不动的人。

branches.en: Pain caused by one's own act becomes apology.
branches.cn: 由自己行为造成的痛，变成道歉。

branches.en: Pain felt for another person becomes sympathy.
branches.cn: 为他人感到的痛，变成同情。

branches.en: The apology is borrowed to soften a refusal.
branches.cn: 道歉被借用来缓和拒绝。

branches.en: An object that looks painful is itself called sorry.
branches.cn: 看着让人心痛的东西，本身就被称作 sorry。

branches.en: Guilt and sympathy both run on the same ache.
branches.cn: 内疚与同情都跑在同一份疼痛上。

intro.en: Sorry is a native adjective made from a native root with a common adjective ending.
intro.cn: sorry 是本土词根加常见形容词词尾构成的本土形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in sorry; its relatives are Old English words for pain and grief.
latinIntro.cn: sorry 没有拉丁成分，其同族词是表示疼痛与悲伤的古英语词。

items.example: Sar is the root of sorry and sore.
items.exampleCN: sar 是 sorry 与 sore 的词根。

items.example: Sarig is the direct ancestor of sorry.
items.exampleCN: sarig 是 sorry 的直接祖先。

items.example: The ending -y makes an adjective from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把词干变成形容词。

items.example: Sorrily adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: sorrily 在形容词后加了 -ly。

items.example: Sorrier changes y to i before -er.
items.exampleCN: sorrier 在 -er 前把 y 变成 i。

items.example: Sorrow is the noun built on the same root.
items.exampleCN: sorrow 是同一词根上的名词。

items.example: Sore keeps the literal sense of sar.
items.exampleCN: sore 保留了 sar 的字面义。

items.example: The sorr- stem appears in sorrier and sorrily.
items.exampleCN: sorr- 词干出现在 sorrier 与 sorrily 中。

definition_en: a word used to give an affirmative answer or to show agreement
core_image: 下巴向下一顿，头点下去
scene: 老师问有没有人愿意帮忙，后排的男孩举手说愿意。When the teacher asked for a volunteer, the boy at the back raised his hand and said yes.
sceneCN: 这里 yes 是「是、愿意」（第 1 个义项：表示肯定回答）；句意：老师问有没有人愿意帮忙时，后排的男孩举手说了愿意。

derivatives.zh: yes 的口语变体，义为「是啊」
yes 的口语变体，义为「嗯，是」

senses.title: An affirmative answer
senses.definition: used to answer a question in a positive way
senses.definitionCN: 用于对问题作出肯定的回答
senses.example: Are you ready? Yes, I am.
senses.exampleCN: 你准备好了吗？是的，我准备好了。
senses.why: The old form combines yea with so be it, so the core picture is a head nodding down on a decision.
senses.whyCN: 古形式是 yea 与「就这样吧」的结合，所以核心画面是头在决定上点下去。

senses.title: Agreement or permission
senses.definition: used to agree with a suggestion or to give permission
senses.definitionCN: 用于同意某个提议或给予许可
senses.example: Yes, you may borrow my bike.
senses.exampleCN: 可以，你可以借我的自行车。
senses.why: A nod that answers a question also grants a request, which supplies the permission sense.
senses.whyCN: 点头既回答了问题，也等于答应了请求，由此生出「许可、同意」的意思。

senses.title: A reply when called
senses.definition: used to answer when someone calls your name
senses.definitionCN: 别人叫你名字时用来应答
senses.example: Yes, coming in a moment.
senses.why: Answering a call is the smallest form of saying that one is present and agrees to come.
senses.whyCN: 回应一声呼唤，是「我在、我愿意来」最简短的表达。

senses.title: A positive vote or answer
senses.definition: a vote or answer in favour of something, countable as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 赞成某项提案的票或回答，可作可数名词
senses.example: The plan passed with fifty yeses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划以五十张赞成票获得通过。
senses.why: The spoken word becomes a countable thing when votes are counted.
senses.whyCN: 当投票被点算时，说出口的那个词就变成可数的东西。

intro.en: Yes comes from Old English gese, a blend of gea, yea, and si, let it be so.
intro.cn: yes 来自古英语 gese，是 gea（是）与 si（就这样吧）的融合。

items.en: Gea means yes or indeed, and survives in the archaic English word yea.
items.cn: gea 意为「是、确实」，在古旧的英语词 yea 中留存下来。

items.en: Si means let it be so, and supplies the second half of gese.
items.cn: si 意为「就这样吧」，提供 gese 的后半部分。

items.en: Gese combines the two into a single emphatic yes.
items.cn: gese 把两者合成一个语气更强的「是」。

items.en: The form shortens to yes and replaces yea in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 中古英语中缩为 yes，并在日常口语中取代 yea。

items.en: Yes becomes a countable noun for a favourable vote or answer.
items.cn: 现代英语中 yes 成为可数名词，指赞成票或肯定回答。

note.en: Yes has several informal variants, and it stands opposite no in the vocabulary of answers.
note.cn: yes 有若干口语变体，并在回答用语中与 no 相对。

entries.definition: an informal yes
entries.definitionCN: 是啊，是 yes 的口语变体

entries.definition: a quick informal yes
entries.definitionCN: 嗯，是，是 yes 的简短口语变体

entries.definition: an old word for yes, still used in voting
entries.definitionCN: 古旧的「是」，投票时仍使用

entries.definition: certainly, used as a friendly yes
entries.definitionCN: 当然，用作随和的肯定回答

entries.definition: used to agree politely and firmly
entries.definitionCN: 当然可以，语气正式而明确

entries.definition: used to show that you accept a suggestion
entries.definitionCN: 同意，用于表示接受提议

normalIntro.en: The word is a fusion of yea and so be it, which makes the nod easy to picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 yea 与「就这样吧」的融合，点头的画面很容易想见。

normal.en: Yea plus so be it gives yes, an answer that settles the matter.
normal.cn: yea 加「就这样吧」构成 yes，一个把事情定下来的回答。

normal.en: Yeah and yep are relaxed spoken versions of the same word.
normal.cn: yeah 与 yep 是同一个词的轻松口语版。

normal.en: The plural yeses is used when counting votes.
normal.cn: 计票时使用复数 yeses。

normal.en: Say yes to an offer, and say yes to a question.
normal.cn: 接受提议说 say yes，回答问题也说 yes。

normal.en: A yes man agrees with everything the boss says.
normal.cn: a yes man 指对上司什么都说好的人。

abstract.en: Picture a chin dropping once, firmly.
abstract.cn: 想象下巴坚定地点一下。

abstract.en: See a green light coming on at a crossing.
abstract.cn: 想象路口亮起绿灯。

abstract.en: Think of a box being ticked on a form.
abstract.cn: 想在表格上打一个勾。

examples.en: Yes, I would like some tea.
She said yes to the invitation at once.
The vote was twenty yeses and three noes.
examples.cn: 投票结果是二十票赞成、三票反对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耶」——想象听见好消息时喊一声耶，表示肯定；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 gese，由 gea（是）与 si（就这样吧）融合而成。

sensesIntro.en: A single nod of agreement covers answering a question, granting permission, replying to a call, and casting a vote.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示同意的点头，涵盖回答问题、给予许可、应答呼唤以及投出赞成票。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chin dropping once in a firm nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：下巴坚定地点一下。

branches.en: The plain affirmative answer is the base use.
branches.cn: 最基础的用法就是肯定回答。

branches.en: The same nod grants a request, giving the permission sense.
branches.cn: 同一个点头也准许请求，形成许可义。

branches.en: Answering a call is the thinnest form of agreement.
branches.cn: 应答呼唤是「同意」最单薄的形式。

branches.en: Counting these answers turns the word into a vote.
branches.cn: 把这些回答点数，就把这个词变成选票。

branches.en: All are the same yes spoken in different settings.
branches.cn: 三者都是同一个「是」在不同场合说出。

intro.en: Yes is a fused native word, so its parts are historical rather than separable today.
intro.cn: yes 是本土融合词，其成分今天已不可分离。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; both halves are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分，两个部分都来自古英语。

items.meaningCN: 古代加强语气的前缀成分
items.example: Ge- appears at the front of gese.
items.exampleCN: ge- 出现在 gese 的开头。

items.example: Gea survives as the archaic yea.
items.exampleCN: gea 作为古旧的 yea 留存下来。

items.example: Si adds the sense of settling a matter.
items.exampleCN: si 增添了把事定下来的意味。

items.example: Gese is the whole ancestor of yes.
items.exampleCN: gese 是 yes 的完整祖先。

items.example: Yeses counts several favourable answers.
items.exampleCN: yeses 指若干个肯定回答。

items.example: Yeah is a relaxed reshaping of yes.
items.exampleCN: yeah 是 yes 的轻松变体。

items.example: Yep closes the mouth on the same answer.
items.exampleCN: yep 用闭嘴的方式说出同一个回答。

items.example: Yea keeps the older half of the family alive.
items.exampleCN: yea 让词族中较老的那一半延续下来。

definition_en: the pronoun a speaker uses to refer to himself or herself as the subject of a sentence
core_image: 说话人抬起手指向自己的胸口
scene: 清晨的厨房里，孩子拍拍胸口，说自己能端稳那杯牛奶。In the morning kitchen, the child patted his chest and said I can carry that glass of milk.
sceneCN: 这里 I 是「我」（第 1 个义项：第一人称单数主格）；句意：清晨的厨房里，孩子拍拍胸口说「我能端稳那杯牛奶」。

senses.title: The speaker as subject
senses.definition: the pronoun used by a speaker for himself or herself as the subject of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 说话人作句子主语时指自己的代词
senses.example: I live near the river.
senses.why: A speaker needs one short sound to put the self at the front of a sentence, so this pronoun marks who is acting.
senses.whyCN: 说话人需要一个短音把自己放在句子开头，于是这个代词标出动作的发出者。

senses.title: The self as an object of thought
senses.definition: the self or personality that a person thinks about, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 人所思考的自身或人格，作名词使用
senses.example: The poem explores a divided I.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗探讨了一个分裂的自我。
senses.why: Once a person can say I, the same word can be turned around and looked at as a thing, namely the self.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦能说 I，就能把同一个词转过来当作对象来看，也就是「自我」。

senses.title: The letter I and the Roman numeral one
senses.definition: the ninth letter of the English alphabet, also the Roman numeral for one
senses.definitionCN: 英语字母表的第九个字母，也是罗马数字的一
senses.example: Write the answer in capital I.
senses.exampleCN: 请用大写字母 I 写出答案。
senses.why: The Latin letter and the Roman numeral share one stroke, so the same capital sign carries both readings.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁字母与罗马数字共用一笔，因此同一个大写符号兼有两种读法。

intro.en: I is one of the oldest words in English and has been shortened from a longer form over many centuries.
intro.cn: I 是英语中最古老的词之一，在漫长岁月里由更长的形式缩短而来。

items.en: The ancestor form ek already served as the first person pronoun.
items.cn: 祖语形式 ek 已经用作第一人称代词。

items.en: The word appears as ic, still pronounced with a final consonant.
items.cn: 古英语中写作 ic，词尾仍有一个辅音。

items.en: The final sound weakens, and the word is often written as ik or i.
items.cn: 中古英语中词尾音弱化，常写作 ik 或 i。

items.en: Printers settle on the single capital letter I for the pronoun.
items.cn: 近代早期，印刷者把这个代词定为单个大写字母 I。

items.en: The capital I is now the only pronoun written with a capital letter in English.
items.cn: 现代英语中，I 是唯一始终大写的代词。

note.en: I belongs to the first person family, whose forms change with grammatical case.
note.cn: I 属于第一人称词族，其形式随语法格变化。

entries.definition: the object form of the first person pronoun
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称代词的宾格形式

entries.definition: belonging to me, used before a noun
entries.definitionCN: 我的，放在名词前作限定词

entries.definition: the one belonging to me, used without a noun
entries.definitionCN: 我的东西，独立使用不带名词

entries.definition: the same person as the speaker, used for emphasis
a person's own nature or identity
the part of the mind that senses the own identity

normalIntro.en: A single upright stroke stands for the speaker, and the older form ic shows where it came from.
normalIntro.cn: 一根竖立的笔画代表说话人，较早的 ic 说明了它的来历。

normal.en: Old English ic lost its final sound and shrank to I.
normal.cn: 古英语 ic 丢掉词尾音，缩成了 I。

normal.en: I is the only English pronoun that is always capitalised.
normal.cn: I 是英语中唯一永远大写的代词。

normal.en: Me, my and mine are the other faces of the same self.
normal.cn: me、my、mine 是同一个「我」的其他面孔。

normal.en: I'm, I've, I'll and I'd pack a verb into one breath.
normal.cn: I'm、I've、I'll、I'd 把一个动词塞进一口气里。

normal.en: The letter I also stands for the number one in Roman counting.
normal.cn: 字母 I 在罗马计数里还代表数字一。

abstract.en: Picture a finger turning back toward the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指转回来指向胸口。

abstract.en: See one upright stroke standing alone on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象纸面上孤零零立着一根竖笔。

abstract.en: Think of a spotlight that shines only on the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一束只照在说话人身上的聚光。

examples.en: I like apples.
I'm going home now.
My brother and I share a room.
examples.cn: 我和弟弟合住一个房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱」——先说「我」，才谈得上「我爱」；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ic，与德语 ich、拉丁语 ego 同出一支远古印欧语代词。

sensesIntro.en: One short pronoun covers the acting self, the self as a topic, and the written sign that names both.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个短代词同时覆盖行动的我、作为话题的自我，以及书写这个符号本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker pointing a finger at the own chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人把手指指向自己的胸口。

branches.en: The pronoun puts the speaker at the head of the sentence.
branches.cn: 这个代词把说话人放在句子开头。

branches.en: The same self becomes a noun when it is thought about.
branches.cn: 同一个自我被思考时，就成了名词。

branches.en: The written sign also serves as a letter and a number.
branches.cn: 书写符号同时充当字母与数字。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the first person point of view.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立足于第一人称视角。

branches.en: The capital sign names the self and the numeral at once.
branches.cn: 大写符号同时命名自我与数字。

intro.en: I is a native pronoun with no separable affixes, so its parts are historical forms of the same word.
intro.cn: I 是本土代词，没有可分离的词缀，列出的成分是同一个词的历史形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin ego is a distant cousin rather than a source, so no Latin element is built into the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ego 只是远亲而非来源，因此这个词没有拉丁构词成分。

items.example: Ic is the Old English form of the pronoun.
items.exampleCN: ic 是这个代词的古英语形式。

items.example: Ek is the older ancestor behind ic.
items.exampleCN: ek 是 ic 背后更早的祖先形式。

items.example: German ich keeps the old final sound.
items.exampleCN: 德语 ich 保留了古老的词尾音。

items.example: Latin ego belongs to the same old family.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ego 属于同一个古老词族。

items.example: Me is the object form of the same self.
items.exampleCN: me 是同一个自我的宾格形式。

items.example: My stands before a noun.
items.exampleCN: my 放在名词前面。

items.example: Mine stands alone without a noun.
items.exampleCN: mine 独立使用，后面不带名词。

items.example: Myself turns the pronoun back on the speaker.
items.exampleCN: myself 把这个代词转回说话人自身。

definition_en: the pronoun used for the person or people being spoken to
core_image: 说话人把目光和手掌转向对方
scene: 公交车上，售票员把票递过去，说这张是给你的。On the bus, the conductor handed the ticket over and said this one is for you.
sceneCN: 这里 you 是「你」（第 1 个义项：第二人称单数）；句意：公交车上，售票员把票递过去，说这张是给你的。

senses.title: The person spoken to
senses.definition: the pronoun for one person being addressed, used as subject or object
senses.definitionCN: 指一个被称呼的人，可作主语或宾语
senses.example: You can sit here.
senses.why: The speaker turns the whole attention outward, so one short word points at the listener.
senses.whyCN: 说话人把全部注意力转出去，一个短词就指向了听者。

senses.title: More than one listener
senses.definition: the same pronoun used for several people being addressed
senses.definitionCN: 同一个代词用于多个被称呼的人
senses.example: You are all welcome to join us.
senses.exampleCN: 欢迎你们大家都来加入我们。
senses.why: English keeps one form for one listener and many listeners, so the plural meaning is carried by the situation.
senses.whyCN: 英语对一位和多位听者只用同一个形式，复数含义靠语境承担。

senses.title: Any person in general
senses.definition: used to mean people in general rather than one particular listener
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一般的人，而非某个特定的听者
senses.example: You never know what will happen.
senses.exampleCN: 你永远不知道会发生什么。
senses.why: A listener stands in for anyone, so the pronoun stretches from this person to people at large.
senses.whyCN: 听者可以代表任何人，于是这个代词从眼前的人扩展到泛指的人。

senses.title: The real self of a person
senses.definition: a person's true character, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 一个人真实的性格或面目，作名词使用
senses.example: The interview showed the real you.
senses.exampleCN: 这次面试展现了真实的你。
senses.why: When the listener is treated as a topic rather than addressed, the pronoun becomes a noun naming that person.
senses.whyCN: 当听者不再被呼唤而成为话题时，这个代词就变成名词，指那个人本身。

intro.en: You began as a plural object form and gradually took over the singular subject as well.
intro.cn: you 起初是复数的宾格形式，后来逐渐连单数主格也一并取代。

items.en: Ge, pronounced like ye, is the nominative plural meaning you all.
items.cn: ge 读近 ye，是主格复数，意为「你们」。

items.en: Eow is the dative and accusative plural of the same pronoun.
items.cn: eow 是同一代词复数的与格与宾格。

items.en: You spreads from polite address to ordinary singular address.
items.cn: you 从礼貌称呼扩展到普通的单数称呼。

items.en: You displaces ye as the subject form in standard speech.
items.cn: 近代早期，you 在标准口语中取代 ye 成为主格。

items.en: One form now serves both singular and plural, with context doing the work.
items.cn: 现代英语由一个形式兼指单复数，靠语境区分。

note.en: You has possessive and reflexive relatives, and older English kept separate singular and plural forms.
note.cn: you 有所有格与反身形式，古英语还区分单数与复数。

entries.definition: belonging to the person spoken to
entries.definitionCN: 你的；你们的，放在名词前

entries.definition: the thing belonging to you
the same person as the listener
an old singular form of you
an old plural form of you
any person in general, used like a generic you
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何人，用法类似泛指的 you

normalIntro.en: The word turns outward toward the listener and once carried a plural sense only.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词朝外指向听者，早先只表示复数。

normal.en: Old English had ye for you all and thou for one person.
normal.cn: 古英语用 ye 表示你们，用 thou 表示你。

normal.en: You was once the object form of ye.
normal.cn: you 原本是 ye 的宾格形式。

normal.en: Politeness made you spread to one listener.
normal.cn: 礼貌用法让 you 扩展到了单个听者。

normal.en: Your, yours and yourself all grow from the same stem.
normal.cn: your、yours、yourself 都从同一个词干长出来。

normal.en: A generic you means anyone at all.
normal.cn: 泛指的 you 指任何人。

abstract.en: Picture an open palm offered to the person in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摊开的手掌伸向面前的人。

abstract.en: See an arrow leaving the speaker and landing on the listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从说话人飞向听者。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror turned away from the self.
abstract.cn: 想象一面背对自己的镜子。

examples.en: You can sit here.
I will wait for you.
You are all welcome.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优」——每个人都想在你面前表现得更优秀；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 eow，本是 ge（你们）的与格与宾格，后来取代 ye 成为主格。

sensesIntro.en: One pronoun covers a single listener, a group, people in general, and even a person treated as a topic.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个代词覆盖单个听者、一群听者、泛指的人，乃至被当作话题的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker turning eyes and an open palm toward the listener.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人把目光和摊开的手掌转向听者。

branches.en: The basic use points at one person being spoken to.
branches.cn: 基本用法指向一个被称呼的人。

branches.en: The same form reaches a whole group of listeners.
branches.cn: 同一个形式也指向一整群听者。

branches.en: The listener can stand for anyone, which yields the generic sense.
branches.cn: 听者可以代表任何人，于是生出泛指义。

branches.en: Turning the listener into a topic makes the pronoun a noun.
branches.cn: 把听者变成话题，代词就成了名词。

branches.en: All three are the same outward pointing word.
branches.cn: 三者都是同一个朝外指的词。

intro.en: You is a native pronoun, so the listed pieces are historical forms rather than living affixes.
intro.cn: you 是本土代词，所列成分是历史形式而非现代词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin element; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分，其亲属词都属日耳曼语。

items.example: Ge was the old plural subject form.
items.exampleCN: ge 是古老的复数主格形式。

items.example: Eow is the ancestor of modern you.
items.exampleCN: eow 是现代 you 的祖先。

items.example: Ye survived in older literature.
items.exampleCN: ye 在较古老的文学作品中留存。

items.example: Thou was the old singular subject form.
items.exampleCN: thou 是古老的单数主格形式。

items.example: Thee was the object partner of thou.
items.exampleCN: thee 是 thou 的宾格伙伴。

items.example: Your comes before a noun.
items.exampleCN: your 放在名词前面。

items.example: Yours stands without a noun.
items.exampleCN: yours 独立使用，不带名词。

items.example: Yourself turns the pronoun back on the listener.
items.exampleCN: yourself 把这个代词转回听者自身。

definition_en: the pronoun a speaker uses for a group that includes himself or herself
core_image: 几个人并肩站成一排
scene: 雨停了，孩子们从屋檐下跑出来，喊着我们可以回家了。The rain stopped, and the children ran out from under the eaves shouting we can go home now.
sceneCN: 这里 we 是「我们」（第 1 个义项：包括说话人在内的一群人）；句意：雨停后，孩子们从屋檐下跑出来，喊着我们可以回家了。

senses.title: The speaker together with others
senses.definition: the pronoun for a group that includes the speaker and at least one other person
senses.definitionCN: 指包括说话人和至少另一位在内的一群人
senses.example: We live in a small town.
senses.why: The speaker steps from the single self into a group, so the pronoun gathers several people behind one voice.
senses.whyCN: 说话人从单独的自我跨进群体，于是这个代词把几个人聚在同一个声音背后。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: used to mean people in general, especially when sharing a common situation
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人们，尤指共享某种处境时
senses.example: We should protect the earth.
senses.why: A group can widen until it means everyone who shares a problem, which gives the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以扩大到所有面临同一问题的人，于是生出泛指义。

senses.title: The author speaking for a group
senses.definition: used by a writer or speaker to refer to the work or group behind the words
senses.definitionCN: 作者或讲者用来指代文字背后的工作或团体
senses.example: As we showed above, the result is stable.
senses.exampleCN: 正如我们上文所示，结果是稳定的。
senses.why: A single writer speaks with the authority of a team, so we lends the sentence shared responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 单个作者借团队的分量说话，we 便给句子添上共同承担的分量。

intro.en: We is a native Germanic pronoun whose shape has barely changed in a thousand years.
intro.cn: we 是本土日耳曼语代词，一千年来形状几乎没变。

items.en: The ancestor form wiz already means we.
items.cn: 祖语形式 wiz 已经表示「我们」。

items.en: The word appears as we, with a long vowel.
items.cn: 古英语中写作 we，元音较长。

items.en: The spelling settles as we and the vowel shortens in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 we，口语里元音变短。

items.en: We keeps its place as the plural subject pronoun.
items.cn: 近代早期，we 保持复数主格代词的位置。

items.en: We also serves as a general word for people sharing a situation.
items.cn: 现代英语中，we 也用来泛指处境相同的人们。

note.en: We changes case like I, and its meaning shifts between a real group and people in general.
note.cn: we 和 I 一样随格变化，词义也在真实群体与泛指之间移动。

entries.definition: the object form of we
belonging to us
the thing belonging to us
the same group as the speaker
all people, used like a general we
entries.definitionCN: 所有人，用法接近泛指的 we

entries.definition: human beings in general

normalIntro.en: The word gathers the speaker and others into one voice, and its case forms are us, our and ours.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把说话人和别人聚成一个声音，变格形式是 us、our、ours。

normal.en: We is the plural partner of I.
normal.cn: we 是 I 的复数伙伴。

normal.en: Us is the object form, as in help us.
normal.cn: us 是宾格，例如 help us。

normal.en: Our comes before a noun, ours stands alone.
normal.cn: our 放在名词前，ours 独立使用。

normal.en: A general we can mean everyone on the planet.
normal.cn: 泛指的 we 可以指地球上的所有人。

normal.en: Writers use we to share responsibility with a team.
normal.cn: 作者用 we 与团队共同承担责任。

abstract.en: Picture several shoulders pressed into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象几个肩膀并成一条线。

abstract.en: See one voice coming out of many mouths.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张嘴发出同一个声音。

abstract.en: Think of a circle drawn around the speaker and the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圈把说话人和别人都圈进去。

examples.en: We live in a small town.
We should help each other.
We are ready to start.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伟」——我们想一起做伟大的事；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 we，来自祖语 wiz，与德语 wir 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One pronoun covers a real group, people in general, and the voice a writer uses for a team.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个代词覆盖真实群体、泛指的人们，以及作者代表团队发声的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several people standing shoulder to shoulder as one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个人肩并肩站成一条线。

branches.en: The base sense gathers the speaker with at least one other person.
branches.cn: 基本义把说话人与至少另一个人聚在一起。

branches.en: The group widens until it stands for people at large.
branches.cn: 群体扩大，直到代表一般的人们。

branches.en: A writer borrows the group voice to share responsibility.
branches.cn: 作者借群体声音来分担责任。

branches.en: Both senses bind several people into one speaker.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把几个人绑成一个说话人。

branches.en: Inclusion is the thread that runs through both.
branches.cn: 「包含」是贯穿两者的线索。

intro.en: We is a native pronoun with no live affixes, so the items are historical forms and case partners.
intro.cn: we 是本土代词，没有现用词缀，所列条目是历史形式与变格伙伴。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in we; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: we 没有拉丁成分，其亲属词属日耳曼语。

items.example: We kept the same shape from Old English.
items.exampleCN: we 从古英语起就保持同样的形状。

items.example: Wiz is the older ancestor of we.
items.exampleCN: wiz 是 we 更早的祖先。

items.example: German wir is a close cousin.
items.exampleCN: 德语 wir 是近亲。

items.example: Us is the object form of we.
items.exampleCN: us 是 we 的宾格形式。

items.example: Our stands before a noun.
items.exampleCN: our 放在名词前面。

items.example: Ours stands without a noun.
items.exampleCN: ours 独立使用，不带名词。

items.example: Ourselves turns the pronoun back on the group.
items.exampleCN: ourselves 把这个代词转回群体自身。

items.example: We're is the spoken contraction of we are.
items.exampleCN: we're 是 we are 的口语缩写。

definition_en: belonging to the person speaking, used before a noun
core_image: 一只手把东西护在自己身前
scene: 孩子把画举到妈妈面前，说这是我家。The child held the drawing up to his mother and said this is my home.
sceneCN: 这里 my 是「我的」（第 1 个义项：表示所属）；句意：孩子把画举到妈妈面前，说这是我家。

pos.zh: 我的（形容词性物主代词）

senses.title: Belonging to the speaker
senses.definition: showing that something belongs to or is connected with the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物属于说话人或与说话人相关
senses.example: My bag is heavy.
senses.why: The speaker puts a small possessive marker before a thing, and ownership is claimed in one syllable.
senses.whyCN: 说话人在事物前放一个小的所属标记，一个音节就认领了归属。

senses.title: Affectionate address
senses.definition: used before a name or title to show warmth or affection
senses.definitionCN: 用在名字或称呼前，表示亲切
senses.example: My dear friend, welcome home.
senses.exampleCN: 我亲爱的朋友，欢迎回家。
senses.why: Close possession of a person softens into affection, so the same word becomes a warm form of address.
senses.whyCN: 把人当作亲近的所属，这种意味软化成亲昵，于是同一个词成了温暖的称呼。

senses.title: An exclamation of surprise
senses.definition: used in phrases such as my goodness to express surprise
senses.definitionCN: 用于 my goodness 一类短语，表示惊讶
senses.example: My goodness, it is cold today.
senses.why: A sudden feeling seizes the speaker so completely that it is voiced as a possession, as if the shock were the speaker's own.
senses.whyCN: 突如其来的感受完全攫住说话人，于是被说成一种所属，仿佛惊讶归自己所有。

intro.en: My is the possessive form of I, and it has kept a short shape since Old English.
intro.cn: my 是 I 的所有格形式，自古英语起就保持短小的形状。

items.en: The ancestor form minaz marks what belongs to the speaker.
items.cn: 祖语形式 minaz 标记属于说话人的东西。

items.en: The possessive appears as min, used before nouns.
items.cn: 古英语中所有格写作 min，放在名词前。

items.en: The final consonant drops, and mi and my compete in writing.
items.cn: 中古英语中词尾辅音脱落，mi 与 my 在书写中并存。

items.en: My wins as the form used before nouns.
items.cn: 近代早期，my 成为名词前使用的定式。

items.en: Mine survives separately as the possessive pronoun.
items.cn: 现代英语中 mine 单独留存为名词性物主代词。

note.en: My is one member of the possessive set, and its standalone partner is mine.
note.cn: my 是物主词族的一员，其独立使用的伙伴是 mine。

entries.definition: the thing belonging to me, used alone
the object form of I
the subject form of the first person pronoun
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称代词的主格形式

entries.definition: belonging to the listener
entries.definitionCN: 你的，同一类物主限定词

entries.definition: belonging to us
entries.definitionCN: 我们的，同一类物主限定词

entries.definition: belonging to them
entries.definitionCN: 他们的，同一类物主限定词

normalIntro.en: My is the shortest way to claim a thing, and mine is the same claim made alone.
normalIntro.cn: my 是认领一样东西最短的方式，mine 是同一个认领独立成句。

normal.en: My comes before a noun, as in my coat.
normal.cn: my 放在名词前，例如 my coat。

normal.en: Mine replaces both my and the noun.
normal.cn: mine 同时替代 my 和名词。

normal.en: My dear is warm, my goodness is surprised.
normal.cn: my dear 表示亲切，my goodness 表示惊讶。

normal.en: Old English min lost its final sound to become my.
normal.cn: 古英语 min 丢掉词尾音，变成了 my。

normal.en: In my view marks an opinion politely.
normal.cn: in my view 礼貌地引出个人看法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand curved around a small object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手弯起来护住一件小东西。

abstract.en: See a name tag written in the speaker's own hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由说话人亲笔写下的名牌。

abstract.en: Think of a circle drawn tightly around one person.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只把一个人紧紧圈住的圆。

examples.en: My bag is heavy.
This is my seat.
My goodness, it is cold!

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买」——我的东西是我自己买的；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 min，与拉丁语 meus、德语 mein 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The same small word claims an object, warms an address, and voices a sudden surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个短词既能认领物品，也能温暖称呼，还能喊出突如其来的惊讶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held protectively in front of a possession.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手护在自己的东西前面。

branches.en: The base sense marks an object as belonging to the speaker.
branches.cn: 基本义把物品标为属于说话人。

branches.en: The same claim, turned on a person, becomes affection.
branches.cn: 同一个认领转向人，就成了亲昵。

branches.en: Strong feeling is voiced as though it were a possession.
branches.cn: 强烈的感受被说成仿佛是一种所属。

branches.en: Ownership and closeness share one root.
branches.cn: 所属与亲近共用一个根源。

branches.en: Both extend the idea of what is mine.

latinIntro.en: Latin meus is a cognate rather than a source, so no Latin element is built into the word.

items.example: Latin meus belongs to the same old family.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 meus 属于同一个古老词族。

items.example: Mine stands alone without a noun.
items.exampleCN: mine 独立使用，不带名词。

items.example: Me is the object partner of I.
items.exampleCN: me 是 I 的宾格伙伴。

items.example: Myself turns the pronoun back on the speaker.
items.exampleCN: myself 把这个代词转回说话人自身。

items.example: The my- stem appears in myself.
items.exampleCN: my- 词干出现在 myself 中。

definition_zh: 名字；名称；名声；给……命名；说出……的名字
definition_en: the word by which a person or thing is known, or to give such a word to someone
core_image: 手指点在一个写着字的标签上
scene: 新生在教室门口停下，老师低头问他的名字。The new pupil stopped at the classroom door, and the teacher looked down and asked for his name.
sceneCN: 这里 name 是「名字」（第 1 个义项：人或物的名称）；句意：新生在教室门口停下，老师低头问他的名字。

pos.zh: 给……命名；说出……的名字；任命

senses.title: The word that identifies someone
senses.definition: the word or words by which a person or thing is known and addressed
senses.definitionCN: 用来称呼和辨认某人或某物的词
senses.example: Her name is Lily.
senses.why: A person needs one short label that others can call out, so the word itself becomes the handle of identity.
senses.whyCN: 人需要一个能被别人叫出口的短标签，于是这个词本身成了身份的把手。

senses.title: Reputation or title
senses.definition: the reputation a person or group has, or the title of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或团体拥有的名声，或事物的名称
senses.example: The company made a name for itself in tea.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在茶叶上闯出了名声。
senses.why: When people repeat a label often enough, the label carries the group's reputation as well as its identity.
senses.whyCN: 当一个标签被反复提起，它就不仅承载身份，也承载这个团体的名声。

senses.title: To give a name
senses.definition: to give a name to a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 给某人、某地或某物起名字
senses.example: They named the baby after his grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用祖父的名字给孩子取名。
senses.why: If a name is a handle, the act of naming is handing that handle to someone for the first time.
senses.whyCN: 如果名字是把手，命名就是第一次把这个把手交到某人手里。

senses.title: To say the name or appoint
senses.definition: to state a name openly, or to appoint someone to a position
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出名字，或任命某人担任某职
senses.example: She was named manager last week.
senses.why: Speaking a name in public puts that person forward, and an official announcement turns the act into an appointment.
senses.whyCN: 当众说出一个名字就是把那个人推举出来，正式宣布则使这一动作变成任命。

intro.en: Name is an old Germanic word whose Latin and Greek cousins share the same ancient root.
intro.cn: name 是古老的日耳曼语词，其拉丁语与希腊语亲属共享同一远古词根。

items.en: The ancestor form namo already means name.
items.cn: 祖语形式 namo 已经表示「名字」。

items.en: The word appears as nama and is used for people, places and things.
items.cn: 古英语中写作 nama，用于人、地点和事物。

items.en: The final vowel weakens and the spelling settles as name.
items.cn: 中古英语中词尾元音弱化，拼写定为 name。

items.en: The verb to name extends from labelling to appointing.
items.cn: 动词 to name 从贴标签扩展到任命。

items.en: Name also stands for reputation, as in making a name.
items.cn: 现代英语中 name 也指名声，如 make a name。

note.en: Name has look-alike relatives built on the same stem and near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: name 有同一词干构成的形近词，也有意思相近的邻居。

entries.definition: used to introduce a more exact statement
entries.definitionCN: 即；也就是，由 name 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: having no name or not known by name
to give a new name to something
the name of a book, film or position
a small word or tag attached to a thing
to give someone a name in speech

normalIntro.en: A name is a handle people can call out, and from it grow naming, renaming and fame.
normalIntro.cn: 名字是一个能被叫出口的把手，命名、改名与名声都由它生长出来。

normal.en: A first name is given, a last name is inherited.
normal.cn: first name 是取的名，last name 是继承的姓。

normal.en: To name a baby is to hand over a handle.
normal.cn: 给婴儿取名，就是交给他一个把手。

normal.en: Make a name means build a reputation.
normal.cn: make a name 意为建立名声。

normal.en: Nameless means no name is known.
normal.cn: nameless 意为无人知道名字。

normal.en: Namely introduces a more exact name for what came before.
normal.cn: namely 为前面的话引出更确切的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a paper tag tied to a suitcase handle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸牌系在行李箱把手上。

abstract.en: See a hand writing one word on a blank line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在空白横线上写下一个词。

abstract.en: Think of a roll call where each answer is a name.
abstract.cn: 想象点名时每一声应答都是一个名字。

examples.en: Her name is Lily.
They named the baby after his grandfather.
examples.cn: 他们用祖父的名字给孩子取名。

examples.en: The town made a name for its tea.
examples.cn: 这个镇子因茶叶而出了名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内姆」——名字里藏着一个人的内幕；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 nama，与拉丁语 nomen、希腊语 onoma 同出一支印欧语词根，意为「名称」。

sensesIntro.en: A name identifies, earns reputation, and turns into the act of naming or appointing.
sensesIntro.cn: 名字既能标识身份、积累名声，也能转化为命名或任命的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger touching a written label.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指点在一个写着字的标签上。

branches.en: The base sense is the word that identifies a person or thing.
branches.cn: 基本义是标识人或物的那个词。

branches.en: A repeated label accumulates reputation.
branches.cn: 被反复提起的标签会积累名声。

branches.en: Handing over the label is the act of naming.
branches.cn: 把标签交出去，就是命名的动作。

branches.en: Saying a name publicly can put a person into a post.
branches.cn: 公开说出名字可以把一个人推上职位。

branches.en: All four grow from one handle that others can use.
branches.cn: 四者都从同一个可供他人使用的把手生长出来。

intro.en: Name is a native stem that takes English endings such as -less, -ly and re-.
intro.cn: name 是本土词干，可接 -less、-ly、re- 等英语词缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun nomen is a cousin of name, not a component of it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 nomen 是 name 的同源亲属，而非其构词成分。

items.example: Nama is the Old English ancestor of name.
items.exampleCN: nama 是 name 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Namo is the older form behind nama.
items.exampleCN: namo 是 nama 背后更早的形式。

items.example: Latin nomen shares the same ancient root.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 nomen 共享同一古老词根。

items.example: Greek onoma is another cousin of name.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 onoma 是 name 的另一个亲属。

items.example: Nameless means having no name.
items.exampleCN: nameless 意为没有名字的。

items.example: Rename means give a new name again.
items.exampleCN: rename 意为重新给一个名字。

items.example: Namely introduces an exact name.
items.exampleCN: namely 引出确切的名字。

items.meaningCN: 过去式或过去分词词尾
items.example: Named marks the past tense of the verb.
items.exampleCN: named 标记动词的过去式。

latinEntries.example: Nomen belongs to the same Indo-European root.
latinEntries.exampleCN: nomen 属于同一个印欧语词根。

definition_zh: 一（个）；每一；字母 A；A 级
definition_en: used before a singular countable noun to mean one unspecified thing, or to mean each
core_image: 伸出一根手指竖在一样东西前面
scene: 清晨的窗台外，一只小鸟停下来，歪头看着屋里。A small bird landed on my windowsill and tilted its head toward the room.
sceneCN: 这里 a 是「一个」（第 1 个义项：不定冠词，指不特定的一件东西）；句意：清晨的窗台外，一只小鸟停下来，歪头看着屋里。

derivatives.zh: a 在元音音素前的变体
名流名单，A 指最高等级
英国高中高级水平考试，A 指等级

senses.title: One unspecified thing
senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun to mean one unspecified person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在可数名词单数前，表示一个不特定的人或物
senses.example: A cat sat by the door.
senses.why: The numeral one weakens into a light sound, so the speaker can mention a single thing without pointing at it.
senses.whyCN: 数字「一」弱化成轻轻的一声，于是说话人提到一样东西却不必特指。

senses.title: Each or per
senses.definition: used before a unit to mean each or per
senses.definitionCN: 用在单位前，表示每一
senses.example: Take the medicine twice a day.
senses.why: One unit is taken as the sample, so a day stands for every day in the same pattern.
senses.whyCN: 取一个单位作样本，于是一天就代表按同样节奏重复的每一天。

senses.title: The letter A and the top grade
senses.definition: the first letter of the English alphabet, also the highest grade in many schools
senses.definitionCN: 英语字母表的第一个字母，也指许多学校中的最高等级
senses.example: She got an A in art.
senses.why: The first letter naturally marks the first and best rank, so the sign shifts from alphabet to grade.
senses.whyCN: 第一个字母自然标记第一与最优，于是这个符号从字母转为等级。

intro.en: The article a is a worn-down form of the old word for one.
intro.cn: 冠词 a 是古词「一」磨损后的形式。

items.en: An means one and is still pronounced with a full vowel.
items.cn: an 意为「一」，元音仍读得完整。

items.en: In fast speech the numeral weakens to a light an before nouns.
items.cn: 中古英语口语中，这个数词在名词前弱读成轻轻的 an。

items.en: Before a consonant the final n drops, giving a.
items.cn: 在辅音前词尾 n 脱落，产生 a。

items.en: The pair a and an settles into the modern pattern.
items.cn: a 与 an 的分工固定为现代格局。

items.en: A also means per, as in twice a day.
items.cn: 现代英语中 a 还表示「每一」，如 twice a day。

note.en: A is the indefinite article, and it stands beside the definite article and the numeral one.
note.cn: a 是不定冠词，与定冠词和数词 one 相邻。

entries.definition: the form of a used before a vowel sound
entries.definitionCN: a 在元音音素前的变体

entries.definition: used for a thing already known to the listener
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词，指听者已知的事物

entries.definition: the number 1
an unspecified amount or number
one or some, used in questions and negatives
entries.definitionCN: 任何一个，用于疑问和否定

entries.definition: for each
entries.definitionCN: 每一，与表示「每」的 a 相近

normalIntro.en: A is the faintest breath of the word one, used when the exact thing does not matter.
normalIntro.cn: a 是 one 最轻的一口气，用在具体是哪一样并不重要时。

normal.en: Before a consonant say a, before a vowel say an.
normal.cn: 辅音前说 a，元音前说 an。

normal.en: A cat means one cat, not a particular cat.
normal.cn: a cat 指一只猫，而不是特定的那只。

normal.en: Twice a day means twice every day.
normal.cn: twice a day 意为每天两次。

normal.en: A is also the first letter and the top grade.
normal.cn: A 还是第一个字母和最高等级。

normal.en: A-list and A-level both build on the idea of top rank.
normal.cn: A-list 与 A-level 都建立在最高等级的观念上。

abstract.en: Picture one finger raised before a single object.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指竖在一样东西前面。

abstract.en: See a blank space where the exact name could go.
abstract.cn: 想象一个可以填确切名字的空位。

abstract.en: Think of a single drop rather than a whole cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水，而不是一整杯。

examples.en: A cat sat by the door.
She read a book in an hour.
examples.cn: 她一小时就读完了一本书。

examples.en: He got an A in art.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊」——看到一样东西先「啊」一声；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 an（一）的弱读形式，辅音前写作 a，元音前写作 an。

sensesIntro.en: One small article covers a single unknown thing, a rate of each, and the top grade of the alphabet.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个小小的冠词覆盖不特定的一件东西、每一的比率，以及字母表中的最高等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger standing before a single object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指竖在一样东西前面。

branches.en: The base sense names one thing without identifying it.
branches.cn: 基本义提到一样东西而不指明是哪样。

branches.en: Taking one unit as a sample gives the sense of each.
branches.cn: 取一个单位作样本，就生出「每一」的意思。

branches.en: The first letter grows into the mark of the best rank.
branches.cn: 第一个字母长成最高等级的标记。

branches.en: Both rest on the number one.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在数字一之上。

branches.en: The single thing and the single letter are both singled out.
branches.cn: 单独的一件东西与单独的字母都被单独标出。

intro.en: A has no living affixes, so the items trace the history of the article and its close compounds.
intro.cn: a 没有现用词缀，所列条目追溯冠词的历史及其常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin unus, meaning one, is a distant cognate of the old Germanic numeral behind a.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus（一）是 a 背后古老日耳曼数词的远亲。

items.example: An is the full old form of the article.
items.exampleCN: an 是这个冠词完整的古老形式。

items.example: A comes before a consonant sound.
items.exampleCN: a 用在辅音音素前。

items.example: An comes before a vowel sound.
items.exampleCN: an 用在元音音素前。

items.example: One keeps the full form of the old numeral.
items.exampleCN: one 保留了古老数词的完整形式。

items.example: A is the first sign of the alphabet.
items.exampleCN: A 是字母表的第一个符号。

items.example: A-list uses A for the highest rank.
items.exampleCN: A-list 用 A 表示最高等级。

items.example: A-level marks an advanced grade.
items.exampleCN: A-level 标记高级等级。

items.example: A-grade keeps the letter as a rank mark.
items.exampleCN: A-grade 把这个字母当作等级标记。

definition_zh: 这；那（定冠词，特指已知的人或物）
definition_en: used before a noun that the listener can identify, or before something unique
core_image: 手指稳稳地点在已经认得的那件东西上
scene: 她进门后把钥匙放在架子上，顺手关掉了灯。She came in, put the key on a shelf, and turned off a lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 the 是「这个」（第 1 个义项：特指双方已知的事物）；句意：她进门后把钥匙放在架子上，顺手关掉了灯。

derivatives.zh: 与 the 同出古英语指示词干，义为「这个」
与 the 同出古英语指示词干，义为「那个」
与 the 同出指示词干，义为「那里」

senses.title: A thing already known
senses.definition: used before a noun that the listener can identify from the situation or from what was already said
senses.definitionCN: 用在听者能从情境或前文辨认出的名词前
senses.example: The book on the desk is mine.
senses.why: The speaker and listener already share which thing is meant, so the article points rather than introduces.
senses.whyCN: 说话人和听者已经知道指的是哪一样，于是这个冠词是在指认而不是介绍。

senses.title: Something unique
senses.definition: used before a noun that is unique in the situation, such as the sun or the sky
senses.definitionCN: 用在情境中唯一的事物前，如太阳、天空
senses.example: The sun rose behind the hills.
senses.why: If only one such thing exists in view, the article simply marks that uniqueness.
senses.whyCN: 如果视野中只有一样这样的东西，冠词只是标出它的唯一性。

senses.title: A whole class of people
senses.definition: used before an adjective to name a whole class of people
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词前，指一整类人
senses.example: The rich should help the poor.
senses.why: One adjective after the article stands for every member of a class, so the phrase means the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 冠词后的一个形容词代表一类中的每个成员，于是这个短语指整个群体。

senses.title: The highest or a particular rank
senses.definition: used before superlatives and ordinal words to mark the highest or a particular rank
senses.definitionCN: 用在最高级和序数词前，标记最高或特定次序
senses.example: This is the best tea in town.
senses.why: A highest rank is unique by definition, so the definite article naturally accompanies it.
senses.whyCN: 最高等级按定义就是唯一的，所以定冠词自然与它同行。

intro.en: The began as a set of demonstratives meaning that, and it slowly became the one definite article.
intro.cn: the 起初是一组意为「那个」的指示词，后来慢慢变成唯一的定冠词。

items.en: Se, seo and thaet are demonstratives that agree with gender and case.
items.cn: se、seo、thaet 是随性与格变化的指示词。

items.en: One form, the, replaces the whole set before nouns.
items.cn: 中古英语中，一个形式 the 取代了整套变格形式。

items.en: The plus an adjective comes to name a whole class.
items.cn: the 加形容词开始指称一整类人。

items.en: The is fixed as the definite article in standard English.
items.cn: 近代早期，the 在标准英语中固定为定冠词。

items.en: The also appears in comparative phrases such as the more the better.
items.cn: 现代英语中，the 还出现在 the more the better 一类比较结构里。

note.en: The points to what is known, while a and some leave the identity open.
note.cn: the 指向已知的事物，而 a 与 some 让身份保持开放。

the thing farther from the speaker
the plural of this
one thing not yet identified

normalIntro.en: The is a pointing word that assumes the listener already knows the target.
normalIntro.cn: the 是一个指认词，默认听者已经知道所指。

normal.en: Say the book when both people know which book.
normal.cn: 双方都知道是哪本书时，说 the book。

normal.en: The sun is unique, so it always takes the.
normal.cn: 太阳是唯一的，所以总用 the。

normal.en: The rich means rich people as a class.
normal.cn: the rich 指作为一类人的富人。

normal.en: Superlatives take the because the top is one.
normal.cn: 最高级前用 the，因为顶点只有一个。

normal.en: The more the better repeats the for a ratio.
normal.cn: the more the better 用两个 the 表示比例。

abstract.en: Picture a finger resting on one known object.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指停在一件已知的东西上。

abstract.en: See a spotlight aimed at a single spot on a stage.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯只打在舞台的一点上。

abstract.en: Think of a box already ticked on a list.
abstract.cn: 想象清单上一个已经打勾的方框。

examples.en: The book on the desk is mine.
The sun rose behind the hills.
This is the best tea in town.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「这」——the 与「这」同义，都指向眼前已知的东西；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语指示词 se、seo、thaet 的弱化合并形式。

sensesIntro.en: One article marks what is known, what is unique, a whole class, and the highest rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个冠词标记已知之物、唯一之物、一整类人以及最高等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger resting on the one object already recognised.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指稳稳点在那件已经被认出的东西上。

branches.en: The base sense points at something both people can identify.
branches.cn: 基本义指向双方都能辨认的东西。

branches.en: Being the only one makes a thing definite by itself.
branches.cn: 作为唯一之物，本身就使它成为定指。

branches.en: An adjective under the article stands for a whole class.
branches.cn: 冠词下的形容词代表一整类。

branches.en: The top rank is unique and therefore takes the same article.
branches.cn: 最高等级唯一，因此也使用同一个冠词。

branches.en: All three depend on the listener being able to fix the referent.

definition_en: used for a person or thing near the speaker, or for something just mentioned
core_image: 手指点在自己手边那样东西上
scene: 孩子拉住妈妈的手，指着身上说这是新外套。The child took his mother by the hand, pointed at himself and said this is my new coat.
sceneCN: 这里 this 是「这」（第 1 个义项：近指单数）；句意：孩子拉住妈妈的手，指着身上说这是他的新外套。

derivatives.zh: this 的复数形式，义为「这些」

senses.title: The thing near the speaker
senses.definition: used for a person or thing near the speaker in space or time
senses.definitionCN: 指空间或时间上离说话人近的人或物
senses.example: This cup is hot.
senses.why: The speaker points to something within reach, so a short word with a tight sound marks closeness.
senses.whyCN: 说话人指向触手可及的东西，一个短促的词就标记了靠近。

senses.title: What has just been said
senses.definition: referring to something just said or happening now
senses.definitionCN: 指刚刚说过或正在发生的事
senses.example: This is what I mean.
senses.why: What has just been said stays close in the conversation, so the near word takes it up.
senses.whyCN: 刚说出口的话在对话里仍算「近」，于是近指词把它接住。

senses.title: So or this much
senses.definition: used before an adjective or adverb to mean so or this much
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词或副词前，表示这么、如此
senses.example: I did not know it was this cold.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道天气会这么冷。
senses.why: The speaker measures the quality against the present point, so closeness becomes degree.
senses.whyCN: 说话人以眼前这一点为尺度，于是「近」转化为程度。

intro.en: This is the near demonstrative of English, and it once had separate forms for each gender.
intro.cn: this 是英语的近指指示词，早先还分性别各有形式。

items.en: The forms thes, theos and this mark the near thing in each gender.
items.cn: thes、theos、this 分别标记各性中的近指事物。

items.en: This becomes the common form for all genders.
items.cn: 中古英语中 this 成为各性通用的形式。

items.en: These develops as the plural partner of this.
items.cn: these 发展为 this 的复数伙伴。

items.en: This is fixed as the near demonstrative in standard English.
items.cn: 近代早期，this 固定为标准英语的近指词。

items.en: This also extends to degree, as in this cold.
items.cn: 现代英语中 this 还延伸到程度，如 this cold。

note.en: This pairs with these in number and with that in distance.
note.cn: this 在数上与 these 配对，在距离上与 that 相对。

normalIntro.cn: this 指向近处的东西，它的复数是 these。

normal.en: This for one near thing, these for several.
normal.cn: 近处一样东西用 this，几样用 these。

normal.en: This and that form the near and far pair.
normal.cn: this 与 that 构成近与远的一对。

normal.en: This can point at what was just said.
normal.cn: this 可以指刚刚说过的话。

normal.en: This cold means so cold.
normal.cn: this cold 意为这么冷。

normal.en: This morning and this time both place the moment near.
normal.cn: this morning 与 this time 都把时刻放在近处。

abstract.cn: 想象手指敲着就在手边的东西。

abstract.en: See a short arrow pointing at the speaker's feet.
abstract.cn: 想象一支短箭头指向说话人的脚边。

abstract.en: Think of a circle drawn tightly around the present moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一个紧紧圈住此刻的圆。

root: 古英语指示词 thes、theos、this 的合并形式。

sensesIntro.en: The near word covers one thing at hand, a statement just made, and a degree held up for comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个近指词覆盖手边的一件东西、刚说出的一句话，以及用来比较的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping the object right at hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指点着就在手边的那件东西。

branches.en: The base sense marks a single thing close to the speaker.
branches.cn: 基本义标记离说话人很近的一件东西。

branches.en: Something just said is also close, so this takes it up.
branches.cn: 刚说出口的话也很近，于是 this 把它接住。

branches.en: Closeness to a point of comparison turns into degree.
branches.cn: 与比较点的接近转化为程度。

branches.en: Both rest on the idea of what is near.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在「近」的观念上。

branches.en: Space and degree are measured from the same near point.
branches.cn: 空间与程度都从同一个近点量起。

intro.en: This is a native demonstrative, so the items trace the family it belongs to.

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is present; the whole family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分，整个词族都属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 那；那个；……的（关系代词）；引导从句
definition_en: used for a person or thing farther away, or to introduce a clause
core_image: 手臂伸向远处指着那样东西
scene: 孩子指着靠墙的一把椅子，说那是他的座位。The child pointed to a chair against the wall and said that is my seat.
sceneCN: 这里 that 是「那」（第 1 个义项：远指单数）；句意：孩子指着靠墙的一把椅子，说那是他的座位。

derivatives.zh: that 的复数形式，义为「那些」
that is 或 that has 的缩写

senses.title: The thing farther away
senses.definition: used for a person or thing farther from the speaker in space or time
senses.definitionCN: 指空间或时间上离说话人较远的人或物
senses.example: That house has a red roof.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋房子有红色的屋顶。
senses.why: The speaker points to something farther away, so the word opens the mouth and stretches the distance.
senses.whyCN: 说话人指向较远的东西，这个词张口发音，把距离拉长。

senses.title: Something already past or mentioned
senses.definition: referring to something already mentioned or already completed
senses.definitionCN: 指已经提到或已经完成的事
senses.example: That was a good idea.
senses.why: Something already past sits at a distance, so the far word marks it.
senses.whyCN: 已经过去的事落在远处，于是远指词标记它。

senses.title: The relative pronoun
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that describes a noun
senses.definitionCN: 引导描述名词的从句
senses.example: The book that I read was short.
senses.why: The word reaches back to a noun and attaches a clause to it, like a far finger pointing at that noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词回指一个名词，把从句挂上去，像远远指着那个名词的手指。

senses.title: The clause connector
senses.definition: used to introduce a statement after verbs such as know or say
senses.definitionCN: 用在 know、say 等动词后引导一个陈述
senses.example: I know that she is right.
senses.why: The far demonstrative weakens into a light connector that carries the clause forward.
senses.whyCN: 远指词弱化成轻巧的连接词，把从句往前带。

intro.en: That is the far demonstrative of English and also the source of a common clause connector.
intro.cn: that 是英语的远指指示词，也是常见从句连接词的来源。

items.en: Thaet marks a thing at a distance and agrees with gender and case.
items.cn: thaet 标记远处的事物，并随性与格变化。

items.en: That becomes the single far form and also begins to introduce clauses.
items.cn: 中古英语中 that 成为唯一的远指形式，并开始引导从句。

items.en: Those develops as the plural partner of that.
items.cn: those 发展为 that 的复数伙伴。

items.en: That is fixed as demonstrative, relative pronoun and conjunction.
items.cn: 近代早期，that 固定为指示词、关系代词和连词。

items.en: The connector that is often left out in speech.
items.cn: 现代英语口语中，连接词 that 常被省略。

note.en: That contrasts with this in distance and with those in number.
note.cn: that 在距离上与 this 相对，在数上与 those 配对。

branches.cn: 过去的事同样在远处，于是 that 把它接住。

intro.cn: that 是本土指示词，所列条目追溯其词族与派生形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in that; the family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: that 没有拉丁成分，整个词族属日耳曼语。

definition_en: used to ask about a thing, to mean the thing that, or to express surprise
core_image: 手里托着一个空盒子等人来填
scene: 老师蹲下来，看着新同学问他的名字。The teacher bent down, looked at the new pupil and asked what his name was.
sceneCN: 这里 what 是「什么」（第 1 个义项：疑问代词，询问事物）；句意：老师蹲下来，看着新同学问他的名字是什么。

senses.title: The question word for things
senses.definition: used to ask for information about a thing
senses.definitionCN: 用来询问关于事物的信息
senses.example: What is in the box?
senses.why: The speaker holds an empty slot and asks the listener to fill it, so the word is a question mark in sound.
senses.whyCN: 说话人留出一个空位请对方填补，于是这个词就是声音里的问号。

senses.title: The thing that
senses.definition: used to mean the thing or things that
senses.definitionCN: 意为「……的东西」或「……的事」
senses.example: Tell me what you need.
senses.why: The same empty slot can be filled by a whole clause, so what comes to mean the thing that.
senses.whyCN: 同一个空位可以由整个从句来填，于是 what 意为「……的东西」。

senses.title: An exclamation
senses.definition: used at the start of a phrase to express surprise or strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用在短语开头，表示惊讶或强烈感受
senses.example: What a lovely day!
senses.why: The question word turns into an exclamation when the speaker already knows the answer and only wants to voice surprise.
senses.whyCN: 当说话人其实知道答案、只想喊出惊讶时，疑问词就转为感叹。

intro.en: What belongs to the old interrogative family that also gives who, whom and which.
intro.cn: what 属于古老的疑问词族，who、whom、which 也出自这一族。

items.en: Hwaet asks about a thing and begins with a breathed sound.
items.cn: hwaet 询问事物，开头是一个送气音。

items.en: The spelling settles as what and the old h falls silent.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 what，古老的 h 不再发音。

items.en: What also begins to mean the thing that.
items.cn: what 也开始表示「……的东西」。

items.en: What a plus a noun becomes a common exclamation.
items.cn: what a 加名词成为常见的感叹结构。

items.en: Whatever and whatsoever grow from the same stem.
items.cn: whatever 与 whatsoever 从同一词干生长出来。

note.en: What asks about things, while which chooses among them and who asks about people.
note.cn: what 询问事物，which 在其中选择，who 询问人。

normal.en: What asks about a thing, who asks about a person.
normal.cn: what 问事物，who 问人。

normal.en: Tell me what you need means tell me the thing you need.

abstract.en: Think of a raised eyebrow that expects an answer.

sensesIntro.en: The word opens a question about a thing, absorbs a whole clause, and finally bursts out as an exclamation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先为事物开出疑问，再吸收整个从句，最后还能迸发为感叹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box held out for someone to fill.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个空盒子递出去等人来填。

branches.en: The base sense asks the listener to name a thing.
branches.cn: 基本义请听者说出一样东西。

branches.en: A whole clause can fill the slot, giving the thing that.
branches.cn: 整个从句可以填进空位，于是意为「……的东西」。

branches.en: When the answer is already felt, the same word becomes an exclamation.

branches.en: Question and exclamation share one shape of feeling.

intro.en: What belongs to the interrogative family, and suffixes such as -ever and -soever build new words from it.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in what; the interrogative family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: what 没有拉丁成分，疑问词族属日耳曼语。

items.example: Whose asks about possession.
items.exampleCN: whose 询问所属。

items.example: Which chooses within a known set.

items.example: Whatever adds -ever to what.

items.example: Whatnot closes a list of similar things.

definition_en: used to ask which person, or to introduce a clause about a person
core_image: 手指向人群里那个还没认出来的人
scene: 门铃响了，妈妈擦着手走到门边，问外面是谁。The bell rang, and Mother wiped her hands and walked to the door, asking who was outside.
sceneCN: 这里 who 是「谁」（第 1 个义项：疑问代词，询问人）；句意：门铃响了，妈妈擦着手走到门边，问外面是谁。

senses.title: The question word for people
senses.definition: used to ask which person or people
senses.definitionCN: 用来询问哪个人或哪些人
senses.example: Who is at the door?
senses.why: The speaker points at a person-shaped blank and asks the listener to fill it with a name.
senses.whyCN: 说话人指向一个人形的空位，请听者用名字把它填上。

senses.title: The person that
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause that describes a person
senses.definitionCN: 引导描述某人的从句
senses.example: She is the one who called.
senses.exampleCN: 她就是打电话来的那个人。
senses.why: The same blank attaches to a person and lets a whole clause describe them.
senses.whyCN: 同一个空位附着在一个人身上，让整个从句来描述他。

senses.title: A list of notable people
senses.definition: a list or chart showing who the important people are
senses.definitionCN: 显示重要人物都有谁的名册或图表
senses.example: The party was a who's who of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这场聚会简直是全镇名人的大集合。

definition_en: to direct the eyes toward something, to seem, or the expression on a face
core_image: 目光像一条线射出去，落在一件东西上
scene: 上课铃响了，老师敲敲黑板，让学生先看黑板再动笔。The bell rang, and the teacher tapped the board, telling the class to look at it before writing.
