senses.title: To direct the eyes
senses.definition: to turn the eyes toward something in order to see it
senses.definitionCN: 把目光转向某物以便看见
senses.example: Look at the sky.
senses.why: The eye sends a line outward and settles on a thing, so the verb means directing sight.
senses.whyCN: 目光像一条线射出去，落在一件东西上，所以这个动词意为把视线投过去。

senses.title: To seem
senses.definition: to seem or appear in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 显得、看起来是某种样子
senses.example: She looked tired.
senses.why: What the eye reports about a person becomes a judgement, so looking becomes seeming.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛对一个人报告的样子变成判断，于是「看」转为「显得」。

senses.title: An expression on the face
senses.definition: an expression in the eyes or on the face
senses.definitionCN: 眼神或脸上的表情
senses.example: He gave me a strange look.
senses.why: The act of looking hardens into a thing, namely the expression the look carries.
senses.whyCN: 看这个动作凝结成一样东西，也就是目光所带的神情。

senses.title: To search
senses.definition: to search for something by directing the eyes around
senses.definitionCN: 用目光四处搜寻某物
senses.example: I am looking for my keys.
senses.why: Sight sweeps a space in search of one object, so directing the eyes extends to searching.
senses.whyCN: 目光扫过一片空间去寻找一样东西，于是「看」延伸到「寻找」。

intro.en: Look is a native verb of seeing that later grew the senses of seeming and of a facial expression.
intro.cn: look 是本土的「看」动词，后来长出「显得」与「神情」的意思。

items.cn: locian 意为看、观察。

items.en: Look for extends the verb to searching.

items.en: The noun a look names the expression on a face.
items.cn: 名词 a look 指脸上的神情。

senses.title: To notice with the eyes
senses.definition: to notice something with the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 用眼睛察觉到某物
senses.example: I can see the mountain.
senses.why: An image enters the eye all at once, so the verb names the moment of receiving sight rather than the effort of looking.
senses.whyCN: 画面一下子进入眼睛，所以这个动词命名的是接收到景象的那一刻，而不是看的努力。

senses.title: To understand
senses.definition: to understand something or realize what it means
senses.definitionCN: 理解某事，或意识到它的含义
senses.example: I see what you mean.
senses.why: Understanding arrives like a picture coming into focus, so the word for sight also names insight.
senses.whyCN: 理解就像画面忽然清晰，于是表示视觉的词也用来表示领悟。

senses.title: To meet someone
senses.definition: to meet or visit someone
senses.definitionCN: 与某人见面或拜访
senses.example: She went to see the doctor.
senses.why: Two people come into each other's field of view, so meeting is described with the verb of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 两个人进入彼此的视野，于是用「看见」的动词来描述见面。

senses.title: To experience
senses.definition: to live through or witness an event
senses.definitionCN: 经历或目睹一件事
senses.example: The town saw many changes that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年这个镇子经历了许多变化。
senses.why: A place that watches events pass by is said to see them, so witnessing becomes experiencing.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方看着事件经过，就被说成「看见」了它们，于是目睹延伸为经历。

senses.title: To rest on a seat
senses.definition: to rest with the weight of the body on the buttocks
senses.definitionCN: 以臀部承重地坐着
senses.example: Sit down, please.
senses.why: The body drops and settles onto a surface, so the verb names the moment weight comes to rest.
senses.whyCN: 身体落下来，稳稳压在某个表面上，所以这个动词命名重量安顿下来的那一刻。

senses.title: To be located
senses.definition: to be in a particular place or position
senses.definitionCN: 处于某个地点或位置
senses.example: The village sits at the foot of the hill.
senses.why: A building or village settles on the land the way a body settles on a seat, so the same verb describes location.
senses.whyCN: 房屋或村庄落在土地上，就像身体落在座位上，于是同一个动词也描述位置。

senses.title: To hold a meeting
senses.definition: to hold a meeting or session, especially of a court or committee
senses.definitionCN: 举行会议或开庭，尤指法庭或委员会
senses.example: The committee sits every Monday.
senses.why: Members take their seats to do official business, so sitting together becomes the name of the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 成员各就各位办理公务，于是一起坐下就成了会议本身的名称。

senses.title: To seat someone
senses.definition: to place someone in a seat
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人坐下
senses.example: The host sat us by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 主人安排我们坐在窗边。
senses.why: If sitting is settling onto a seat, the transitive use is causing someone else to settle there.
senses.whyCN: 如果坐是落到座位上，那么及物用法就是让别人落到那里。

examples.en: Sit down, please.
The village sits at the foot of the hill.
They sat in silence.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seat」——sit 与 seat 只差一个音，坐下就是落到座位上；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sittan，与德语 sitzen 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with a body on a seat, then extends to where a place stands and to people meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从身体坐在座位上开始，延伸到地点所在以及人们开会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the body dropping and settling onto a seat.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体落下，稳稳坐在座位上。

branches.en: The base sense is the body coming to rest on a seat.
branches.cn: 基本义是身体在座位上安顿下来。

branches.en: A building settling on land uses the same image.
branches.cn: 建筑落在土地上使用同一幅画面。

branches.en: Members taking their seats becomes the meeting itself.
branches.cn: 成员就座就变成会议本身。

branches.en: Causing someone to sit is the transitive partner.
branches.cn: 让别人坐下是它的及物伙伴。

branches.en: All three share the picture of settling into place.
branches.cn: 三者共享「安顿到位」的画面。

intro.en: Sit is a native stem that forms babysit and takes ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: sit 是本土词干，可构成 babysit，并接普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in sit; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: sit 没有拉丁成分，其亲属词属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 站；站立；坐落；忍受；立场；看台
definition_en: to be on the feet, to be located, to endure, or a position on an issue
core_image: 双脚牢牢踩在地上，身体竖直不动
scene: 上课前，班长喊了一声，全班站起来向老师问好。Before class the monitor called out, and the whole class stood up to greet the teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 stand 是「站」（第 1 个义项：双脚立起、身体竖直）；句意：上课前，班长喊了一声，全班站起来向老师问好。

derivatives.zh: 理解，由 under 与 stand 复合

senses.title: To be on the feet
senses.definition: to be upright on the feet
senses.definitionCN: 双脚直立地站着
senses.example: Please stand up.
senses.why: The feet press into the ground and hold the body upright, so the verb names firm vertical support.
senses.whyCN: 双脚压进地面，把身体撑直，所以这个动词命名的是稳固的竖直支撑。

senses.title: To be located
senses.definition: to be in a particular place or condition
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处或处于某种状态
senses.example: The old tower still stands.
senses.why: A building that stays upright on its ground is said to stand there, so the posture of the body describes where things are.
senses.whyCN: 建筑稳稳立在土地上，就被说成 stand 在那里，于是身体的姿态用来描述事物的位置。

senses.title: To endure
senses.definition: to bear something difficult without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 承受困难而不垮掉
senses.example: I can't stand the noise.
senses.why: Standing firm under a weight becomes the image of enduring something unpleasant.
senses.whyCN: 在重压之下仍站得住，成了忍受不快之事的画面。

senses.title: A position on an issue
senses.definition: a firm opinion or position that someone takes
senses.definitionCN: 某人采取的坚定看法或位置
senses.example: She took a stand against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个计划表明了反对立场。
senses.why: A person who will not move from a spot has a position, and that physical firmness becomes a stated opinion.
senses.whyCN: 一个人不肯离开某个位置，就有了立场，而这种身体的坚定变成公开的看法。

senses.title: A stall or viewing area
senses.definition: a raised structure for watching, or a small stall at a market
senses.definitionCN: 观看用的看台，或集市上的小摊
senses.example: We watched the match from the stand.
senses.why: A structure built to stay in place and hold people becomes a stand, from the same idea of standing firm.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定在那里、承载人群的结构也叫 stand，仍来自「稳稳立住」的观念。

intro.en: Stand is an old Germanic verb of upright posture whose meaning widened to endurance and position.
intro.cn: stand 是古老的日耳曼语直立姿态动词，词义扩展到忍受与立场。

items.en: Standan means to stand or remain upright.
items.cn: standan 意为站立、保持直立。

items.en: The spelling settles as stand and the past form becomes stood.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 stand，过去式成为 stood。

items.en: Stand also means to endure, as in cannot stand.
items.cn: 近代早期，stand 也意为忍受，如 cannot stand。

items.en: A stand becomes a stated position on an issue.
items.cn: 现代英语中，a stand 成为对某事的公开立场。

items.en: A stand also names a market stall or a viewing structure.
items.cn: 现代英语中，stand 还指集市摊位或看台。

note.en: Stand is upright and firm, while sit is settled low and stay is simply remaining.
note.cn: stand 是竖直而稳固，sit 是低处安顿，stay 只是停留。

normalIntro.en: Stand is the body held upright, and the same firmness becomes endurance and a stated position.
normalIntro.cn: stand 是身体被撑直，同一种稳固又变成忍受与公开立场。

normal.en: Stand up is the common call to rise.
normal.cn: stand up 是叫人起身的常用说法。

normal.en: The past tense is stood, the participle stood.
normal.cn: 过去式是 stood，过去分词也是 stood。

normal.en: A tower stands on a hill means it is located there.
normal.cn: 「a tower stands on a hill」意为塔坐落在那里。

normal.en: Cannot stand means cannot endure.
normal.cn: cannot stand 意为无法忍受。

normal.en: Take a stand means state a firm position.
normal.cn: take a stand 意为表明坚定立场。

abstract.en: See a column holding up a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柱子撑起屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a flagpole that will not lean.
abstract.cn: 想象一根不肯倾斜的旗杆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two feet planted firmly on the ground, the body upright.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚牢牢踩地，身体笔直。

branches.en: The base sense is the body held upright on the feet.

branches.en: A building staying upright describes where it is.

branches.en: Standing firm under pressure becomes endurance.

branches.en: Refusing to move from a spot becomes a stated position.
branches.cn: 不肯离开某个位置就变成公开立场。

branches.en: The upright structure and the viewing stand share the same firm shape.
branches.cn: 直立的结构与看台共享同一种稳固形状。
